details.content: t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) is an unsupervised, non-linear technique primarily used for data exploration and visualizing high-dimensional data.

t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding gives an intuition of how data is arranged in high dimensional space by calculating the probability of similarity of points in high-dimensional space and the probability of similarity of points in the corresponding low-dimensional space.

t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding minimizes the difference between conditional probabilities (similarities) in higher-dimensional and lower-dimensional spaces for a perfect representation of data points in lower-dimensional space.
t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding minimizes the sum of Kullback-Leibler divergence of overall data points using a gradient descent method.
Kullback-Leibler divergence measures the difference between two probability distributions.
Kullback-Leibler divergence is minimized in t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding to achieve a faithful low-dimensional representation.
Gradient descent method is an optimization algorithm that iteratively updates parameters in the direction of the negative gradient of a loss function.
Gradient descent method is used to minimize the sum of Kullback-Leibler divergence in t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding.
Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a linear dimensionality reduction technique that projects data onto orthogonal components capturing maximum variance.
PCA is a linear technique, whereas t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding is a non-linear technique.
